annotationWithheld.clue: Sun block from Europe borders on second best

clue.text: Issue diet plan with no one's backing

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange, so the letters of diet are arranged anew
backing means the words no and one are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Distribute an eating regime that nobody supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' rearranges DIET into EDIT; 'backing' turns NO + I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: One printing or version of a publication is an issue of it.

clue.text: Vessel that could be fired

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to carry goods to and from ships
a device that is set alight to give a flame for cigarettes

explanation.definitionFit: A barge for unloading ships has this name, and so does a pocket device that is ignited.

clue.text: Exercise first mate found an annoyance

parts.note: PE is physical education
Eve was Adam's partner, the first wife

explanation.surface: Fitness training first, then a shipmate turned out to be irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' looks nautical but means Eve, the first wife in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate or irritation is a synonym of annoyance.

clue.text: Mushy peas, say, — that's ' simple

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed, so the letters are mashed up

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Mashed peas, for example, are no trouble to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushy' rearranges PEAS and SAY into EASYASP; mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed peas.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very straightforward, no trouble at all.

clue.text: They are often cast as followers

definitions.text: They are often cast as followers

parts.words: They are often cast as followers
parts.note: things thrown on the ground by a body in light, which trail after a person; also an old word for those who tag along behind someone

explanation.surface: A remark about actors who keep getting parts as hangers-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark outline is literally cast by light and follows its owner everywhere, and a follower can be called one.

clue.text: Suddenly starting to pay attention to conman

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word

parts.note: hark means listen, pay attention

explanation.surface: Abruptly beginning to notice a fraudster.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who preys on others is called this predatory fish.

clue.text: Sober, can enter-not here

indicators.note: the can enters, going inside the other word

parts.note: absent means not present
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A teetotaller can't come in because they are away.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'enter-not' is a print slip; 'enter' is the container signal and 'not here' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone refraining from drink is temperate, a synonym of sober.

clue.text: Thinking of nothing, and missing badly

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
pining means longing for something absent

explanation.surface: Thoughts of emptiness and a deep sense of loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding or voicing a view is a synonym of thinking.

clue.text: What to wear and set off this?

definitions.text: What to wear and set off this?

indicators.note: set off suggests the letters going off in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking what clothing to put on before going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WEAR and SET; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper is a garment one puts on before setting out.

clue.text: Reign disrupted by ship's arrival

indicators.note: a reign that is disrupted is thrown into disorder, so its letters are put in a new order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A monarch's rule is upset when a vessel turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' turns REIGN into INGRE; 'by' just places SS beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry or the act of coming in is a synonym of arrival.

clue.text: Sign of a fashionable food additive

parts.note: U means upper-class, hence fashionable or socially acceptable
a seasoning added to food, such as pepper or nutmeg

explanation.surface: Some hint of a stylish seasoning being used in cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen or portent, as when Roman augurs read birds, is a sign.

clue.text: Ignorant tinker had need of translation

indicators.note: words that are in need of translation must be rendered anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A travelling mender needed someone to translate for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need of translation' rearranges the nine letters of TINKER and HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uninformed about something is an idiom of being without light on it.

clue.text: I would start to ignore books — fool!

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone vows to begin neglecting their reading and calls themself a dunce.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton or dimwit is a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Ex PM's point

definitions.meaning: Lord Frederick, Prime Minister of Britain during the American War of Independence
one of the four cardinal points of the compass

explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was a British Prime Minister in the 1770s, and the same name is a compass direction.

clue.text: Stress that drunk is not heavy

parts.note: high means intoxicated
light is the opposite of heavy

explanation.surface: Emphasising that a tipsy person is not overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise or draw attention to is a synonym of stress.

clue.text: One's carried traverse to green, somehow

parts.note: to pass is to go across or through

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of green arranged in some way

explanation.surface: Golf instructions: cross over to the putting surface by whatever route.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in a vehicle who does not drive is conveyed by it.

clue.text: A small quantity might give grounds for arrest

definitions.meaning: a trace or hint, as in a hint of garlic
police may detain someone held to be under reasonable doubt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a slight trace, and reasonable mistrust is the legal basis for detaining someone.

clue.text: Are they duty bound? Hardly!

parts.note: duty here is customs tax; those who bring goods in illegally are certainly not bound to pay it

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether some people are obliged to do their duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband runners avoid paying customs duties, so they are far from bound by them.

clue.text: Picks the groups that take in the Spanish

indicators.note: the groups take in, or contain, the other word

parts.note: sects are religious groups
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Chooses the bands who accept Spaniards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the groups' and 'the Spanish' each keep their 'the': the first gives a plural noun, the second is the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is a synonym of pick.

clue.text: University doctor's anger at offence

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
rage is intense anger

explanation.surface: An academic physician is furious at an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking umbrage means taking offence, feeling resentment.

clue.text: Reduce water supply to queen

parts.note: a tap supplies water from the mains
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut back the water given to the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow gradually or diminish is a synonym of reduce.

clue.text: Object to rubbish being taken in by nuisance

indicators.note: the rubbish is taken in, held inside the nuisance

parts.note: a pest is an annoyance
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: An irritating person objects to garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to raise a complaint or dissent.

clue.text: About to take a bet on editor, but passed it on

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to lay is to place a bet

explanation.surface: Someone bet on the editor and then handed the tip along.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmitted or forwarded a message is passed it on.

clue.text: Be all at sea, though on the case

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Feeling lost even though one is dealing with the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link; the definition is cryptic, since a tag is found on a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag stuck on luggage is what is found on a suitcase.

clue.text: The sweet music of a Vatican drummer?

definitions.meaning: a dessert of sponge cake rolled up with jam
the Pope is guarded by soldiers from Switzerland, so a drumbeat from one of them would be theirs

explanation.surface: Wondering what tune a percussionist at the Vatican plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam-filled sponge cake is a dessert, and a drum roll played by the Pope's Swiss Guard fits the whimsical second reading.

clue.text: Odds about early start to drinking bout

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds in betting
re means about

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter, here of the word early

explanation.surface: The odds around how soon the drinking session starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' is SP, the starting price in betting; 'start to' takes the first letter of 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of indulgence, such as a binge, is a bout.

clue.text: Quiet at the back, Rod!

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
aft means at the stern, the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Telling a man named Rod to be quiet at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole or long bar is a rod.

clue.text: Empty cell-fury at er, rer!

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: fury is extreme anger

explanation.surface: A prisoner is enraged at a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLANGER is a British colloquialism for an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is a British slang word for a glaring blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Metaphors from lines by one wise man

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mage is a magus or learned sage
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Figures of speech written by a single sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language collectively, including metaphors, is called this.

clue.text: Peter's changed round Colin's initial view

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the other piece
the letters of Peter's are changed into another order
Colin's initial is his first letter

explanation.surface: Peter has altered his opinion around a friend's first impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns PETERS into SPETRE, which goes 'round' C.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition or ghostly sight is something seen, a vision.

clue.text: Scored-gallery in agreement

indicators.note: the gallery sits in the word for agreement

parts.note: a nod shows agreement
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An art gallery is in accord with a scoring decision.
explanation.walkthrough: The TATE is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written down in notation is scored.
